title: GAugLLM: Improving Graph Contrastive Learning for Text-Attributed Graphs with Large Language Models

problem.claim: Self-supervised graph learning for text-attributed graphs must generate useful views from textual node attributes while preserving their semantic meaning and leveraging graph structure.

gap.claim: Existing approaches perturb numerical features and topology, while raw text is difficult to perturb without semantic alteration and textual attributes are not inherently well-aligned with graph structure.

contributions.claim: GAugLLM is a framework for augmenting text-attributed graphs with large language models such as Mistral.
A mixture-of-prompt-expert technique adaptively maps prompt-based modifications of raw text attributes into numerical node features.
A collaborative edge modifier uses structural and textual commonalities to examine or build connections between nodes for edge augmentation.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe GAugLLM as a novel framework for augmenting text-attributed graphs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across five benchmark datasets from various domains, the authors report that GAugLLM enhances leading contrastive methods including BGRL, GraphCL, and GBT as a plug-in tool.
The authors report that the augmented features and graph structure also enhance standard generative methods including GraphMAE and S2GAE.
The authors report improved performance for graph neural networks including GCN and GAT.

narrative_sequence.summary: The work studies self-supervised graph learning for graphs whose nodes have textual attributes and motivates this setting by the semantic information in real-world text.
Traditional perturbations and the properties of raw text create difficulties in preserving semantics and aligning text with graph structure.
GAugLLM applies large language models through prompt experts for node-feature augmentation and a collaborative modifier for edge augmentation.
The authors report gains across five benchmark datasets for contrastive, generative, and graph-neural-network methods.
An open-source implementation is reported as available.

source_observation.claim: Text attributes may be difficult to perturb directly because they vary in length and quality, while textual and structural information may be poorly aligned.

interpretation.claim: Augmentation for text-attributed graphs should preserve semantic content while coordinating textual and structural signals.

application.claim: Use language-guided feature augmentation together with structure-aware edge augmentation when designing self-supervised views for text-attributed graphs.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this strategy is effective beyond the reported benchmark setting or for all text-attributed graphs.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify dataset names, evaluation metrics, baseline comparisons, or quantitative effect sizes.
The abstract does not provide implementation details, computational costs, or ablation results.
